appliance.name: Appliance
appliance.corners: The corners are the theme's `shapeScheme`, Appliance's moulded radii by default, held to bands that still read as moulded plastic (a key from 6 to 14, round only). A part takes its own corners from its style's `corners`, a step per corner, start and end as it reads.

brutal.name: Brutal
brutal.corners: Every box is square: no part reads a style's `shape` or `corners`.

civic.name: Civic
civic.corners: Civic's corner steps are 2, 4, 8, 12 and 16, round, each held to a band where Civic still reads as plain and public (`CivicThemeData.shapeLimits`); a field, a select, a row, a table's cell and a notice stay square. A part takes its own corners from its style's `corners`.

clay.name: Clay
clay.corners: `shapeScheme` is the one source of Clay's corners and relief: steps of 6, 9, 16, 24 and 32, each held to Clay's band, and a `depth` that scales how far a part stands. A part takes one step on every corner from its style's `corners`; balls, pills and the dock's places stay round.

comic.name: Comic
comic.corners: Comic is square unless an app rounds it: `shapeScheme` sets the corners, the ink's weight and the print's depth, each held to Comic's band. Start from `comicShapeScheme`, Comic's own. A part takes its own corners from its style's `corners`, none to large at each.

fluent2.name: Fluent 2
fluent2.corners: `shapeScheme` holds Fluent's radius tokens, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 12, which the parts take as a Fluent theme's components do; `Fluent2ThemeData.shapeLimits` holds each to a band where it still reads as Fluent.

frosted.name: Frosted
frosted.corners: `shapeScheme` is the corner scale, held to Frosted's bands. A round corner is drawn at its radius; a superellipse, a bevel or any other is cut to its outline, fill, edge, glass and focus alike.

gloss.name: Gloss
gloss.corners: `shapeScheme` holds Gloss's five corner steps, round fillets of 7, 12, 16, 18 and 24, which the parts take by size. A change of corners eases across with the theme.

keycap.name: Keycap
keycap.corners: A part's corners are fixed (ui_core's `cornerFreedom: fixed`): a keycap's profile is the look, so a style's `corners` leaves them as they are.

ledger.name: Ledger
ledger.corners: Ledger's corner steps are 3, 6, 6, 6 and 12, and what the hand holds (a button, a chip, a field, a search) is round at any height. Each step moves within a band where Ledger still reads as paper (`LedgerThemeData.shapeLimits`).

material_expressive.name: Material Expressive
material_expressive.corners: The theme's corners are M3's five steps, 4, 8, 12, 16 and 28, in `shapeScheme`; an app's own steps are each held to Expressive's band (`ExpressiveThemeData.shapeLimits`), so the scale keeps its order and extra large stays well above large. A part takes its own corners from its style's `corners`, start and end as the text reads, and a press still morphs it on its spring.

minimal.name: Minimal
minimal.corners: `shapeScheme` holds the corners every part reads (4, 8, 10, 14 and 18 by default), each step held to Minimal's band. `MinimalShapes(radius: r).scheme` sets every step from one radius.

neumorphism.name: Neumorphism
neumorphism.corners: `shapeScheme` sets the corners and the depth. No corner is sharp: the smallest is 6, and a face inside another follows the outer corner.

retro_desktop.name: Retro Desktop
retro_desktop.corners: Corners, line widths and shadows belong to the appearance and are not settings: Retro Desktop opens none of ui_core's `RawShapeScheme`. One appearance rounds push buttons, popups and tabs by 4; the other is square everywhere.

studio.name: Studio
studio.corners: The corners are the theme's `shapeScheme`, Studio's milled radii by default, held to bands that still read as milled hardware (a key from 4 to 10, round only). A part takes its own corners from its style's `corners`, a step per corner.

terminal.name: Terminal
terminal.corners: A part's corners are fixed (ui_core's `cornerFreedom: fixed`): a frame's corners are box-drawing cells, `┌ ┐ └ ┘`, so there is no radius to set.
